source_text: ἡττηθῆναι αὐτόν, δόξαν αὐτῷ μᾶλλον ἢ ὕβριν ἔφερεν. Ὅθεν νῦν αὐτὸν διὰ δειλῆς καὶ ταπεινῆς καὶ ἀσθενοῦς σαρκὸς νικῶ, οὐ πειράζων ἀλλὰ πειραζόμενος, οὐ βάλλων ἀλλὰ βαλλόμε νος, οὐκ ἀποκτέννων ἀλλ' ἀποθνῄσκων, οὐ σταυρῶν ἀλλὰ σταυ ρούμενος, οὐ τύπτων ἀλλὰ τυπτόμενος, ἵνα μὴ ἐμοὶ τὰ τῆς νίκης ἐπιγραφῇ, ἀλλ' ἵνα διὰ τῆς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου μορφῆς τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὰ βραβεῖα ἀπονεμηθῇ. ∆ιὰ τοῦτο οὖν δοκῶ δειλιᾶν, ἵνα ὁ μὲν διάβολος ὡς ἰχθὺς ἐπὶ τὸ δέλεαρ πέσῃ, ὁ δὲ θάνατος ὥσπερ στρουθίον τῇ κόλλῃ προσ παγῇ. Ἐπειδὴ γὰρ ἠπάτησεν κακῶς, διὰ τοῦτο ἀπατᾶται καλῶς. Ἐπειδὴ διὰ σωματικὴν ἡδονὴν ἐγοήτευσεν τὸ γένος τῶν ἀνθρώπων, διὰ τοῦτο διὰ σώματος ἀπελαύνεται τοῦ γένους. Ὅπερ ἐποίησεν πάσχει· ὃ εἰς τοὺς πολλοὺς ἔπραξεν, τοῦτο παρ' ἑνὸς ὑπομένει. Ἀλλ' ὃ μὲν ἐποίησεν ἐκεῖνος, τοῖς πεπονθό σιν ὀλέθριον ἦν, ὃ δὲ ἐγὼ εἰς αὐτὸν ποιῶ, τῇ οἰκουμένῃ ἔσται σωτήριον. Ἀπατῶ γὰρ διὰ τοῦ σώματος τὸν πλάνον, ἵνα ἐλεγχ θεὶς μηκέτι δύνηται πλανᾶν οὓς ἐπλάνα αὐτὸς τῷ σώματι· προσ φέρει τὸν θάνατον, ἐγὼ δι' αὐτοῦ παρέχω τὴν ἀνάστασιν. Ἄκων εὐεργετεῖ τὸ γένος. ∆ι' ὧν γὰρ τὸν θάνατον προσάγει, τῆς ἀνα στάσεως πρόφασιν προσάγει. Ὁ πάντων ἐπίβουλος εὐεργέτης τῆς οἰκουμένης γέγονεν ἄφνω· εὐεργέτησεν δὲ τὴν οἰκουμένην πλανηθείς, πλάνην τῷ κόσμῳ συμφέρουσαν καὶ τρόπαιον κατὰ τῆς ἑαυτοῦ τυραννίδος ἐπινοήσας. Ὥσπερ ὁ λίθον ἀκοντίζων κατὰ πέτρας τὴν μὲν πέτραν οὐ διαρρήξει, τὸν δὲ λίθον συντρίψει, οὕτως καὶ ὁ διάβολος κατὰ τοῦ σώματος τοῦ ἐμοῦ ὥσπερ λίθον τὸν θάνατον ῥίψας τὸ μὲν ἐμὸν σῶμα οὐ διέφθειρεν–Οὐ δώσεις γὰρ τὸν ὅσιόν σου ἰδεῖν διαφθοράν–τὰ 5 δὲ ἑαυτοῦ κέντρα συνέθλα σεν τῆς ἀντιτυπίας τὸ στερρὸν ὑπομεῖναι μὴ δυνάμενος. Μηδεὶς οὖν μου δι' ἄγνοιαν δειλίαν καταψηφιζέσθω μηδὲ τα πεινὰ ῥήματα τῇ θεότητι ἐπιριπτέτω. choices.term: δειλῆς καὶ ταπεινῆς καὶ ἀσθενοῦς σαρκὸς
choices.english: fearful and lowly and weak flesh
choices.why: Keeps the three adjectives in their source order and force, matching the glossary's 'fear' for δειλία and the homily's emphasis on Christ's apparent human weakness.
rejected: timid and humble and feeble flesh
cowardly and lowly and weak flesh

choices.why: βραβεῖα are contest prizes; 'assigned' preserves the distributive force of ἀπονεμηθῇ, showing the victory is credited to humanity.

choices.term: ὡς ἰχθὺς ἐπὶ τὸ δέλεαρ πέσῃ
choices.english: like a fish may fall upon the bait
choices.why: Keeps the simile vivid and literal; 'fall upon' preserves πέσῃ, the devil's active lunge onto the bait.
rejected: like a fish may bite the bait
like a fish may be caught by the bait

choices.english: like a sparrow may be stuck to the birdlime
choices.why: κόλλα is specifically birdlime, the sticky substance used to trap birds; 'stuck to' preserves the passive force of προσπαγῇ.
rejected: like a sparrow may be caught in the snare
like a bird may be glued to the lime

choices.english: he deceived badly... he is deceived well
choices.why: The adverb pair κακῶς/καλῶς is the rhetorical hinge; 'badly/well' keeps the moral contrast sharp and literal.
rejected: he deceived wickedly... he is deceived rightly
he deceived for evil... he is deceived for good

choices.term: Ὁ πάντων ἐπίβουλος εὐεργέτης τῆς οἰκουμένης γέγονεν ἄφνω
choices.english: The plotter against all has suddenly become a benefactor of the inhabited world
choices.why: ἐπίβουλος is 'plotter against', not just 'enemy'; 'suddenly' preserves ἄφνω, the paradox of the devil's unintended benefit.
rejected: The enemy of all has become a benefactor of the world
The schemer against all has unexpectedly become a benefactor

pass_b_english: For him to be defeated by me would have brought him glory rather than shame. So now I conquer him through fearful and lowly and weak flesh—not tempting but being tempted, not striking but being struck, not killing but dying, not crucifying but being crucified, not beating but being beaten—so that the victory may not be credited to me, but so that through the form of a human being the prizes may be assigned to the human race. For this reason, then, I seem to fear, so that the devil like a fish may fall upon the bait, and death like a sparrow may be stuck to the birdlime. For since he deceived badly, for this reason he is deceived well. Since through bodily pleasure he bewitched the human race, for this reason through a body he is driven away from the race. What he did, he suffers; what he wrought against the many, this he endures from one. But what that one did was ruinous to those who suffered it, while what I do against him will be salvation for the inhabited world. For I deceive the deceiver through the body, so that once refuted he may no longer be able to deceive those whom he himself deceived through the body. He brings death; through it I provide resurrection. Unwillingly he benefits the race. For through the very things by which he brings death, he brings an occasion for resurrection. The plotter against all has suddenly become a benefactor of the inhabited world. He benefited the inhabited world by being deceived, devising a deception that profits the world and a trophy against his own tyranny. Just as one hurling a stone against a rock will not shatter the rock but will crush the stone, so also the devil, hurling death like a stone against my body, did not destroy my body—for you will not let your holy one see corruption (Psalm 16:10)—but shattered his own stings, unable to withstand the solid resistance. Let no one, then, condemn me for fear out of ignorance, nor hurl lowly words at the divinity. I am a shepherd according to the Word of the divinity. problems.why: Missing 'Unwillingly' at start: the devil benefits the race AGAINST HIS WILL

problems.quote: He brings death; through it I provide resurrection.
problems.source_quote: προσφέρει τὸν θάνατον, ἐγὼ δι' αὐτοῦ παρέχω τὴν ἀνάστασιν.
problems.why: Subject of 'brings death' is the devil, not Christ. English 'He' could be read as Christ.
problems.fix: He brings death; through it I provide resurrection.
problems.ruling: Greek 'προσφέρει' lacks explicit subject; context demands 'the devil' (ὁ διάβολος from prior clause), but English 'He' is ambiguous and risks misreading Christ as subject.

problems.quote: For to be defeated by him would have brought him glory rather than shame
problems.source_quote: ἡττηθῆναι αὐτόν, δόξαν αὐτῷ μᾶλλον ἢ ὕβριν ἔφερεν
problems.why: Subject/object reversed: 'to defeat him' (Christ defeating devil), not 'to be defeated by him'
problems.fix: For to defeat him would have brought him glory rather than shame
problems.ruling: ἡττηθῆναι αὐτόν = 'to defeat him' (aorist passive of ἡττάω with acc.); English reverses meaning.

edits.old: For to be defeated by him would have brought him glory rather than shame.
edits.new: For to defeat him would have brought him glory rather than shame.

fixed: Corrected: 'to be defeated by him' reversed the subject/object of 'ἡττηθῆναι αὐτόν' (to defeat him).
No edit needed: 'Unwillingly he benefits the race' already includes 'Unwillingly' and correctly renders 'Ἄκων εὐεργετεῖ τὸ γένος'.

No edit needed: 'He brings death; through it I provide resurrection' correctly renders 'προσφέρει τὸν θάνατον, ἐγὼ δι' αὐτοῦ παρέχω τὴν ἀνάστασιν'; the subject 'He' is the devil from the preceding context.

problems.quote: what he practiced against the many
problems.why: ἔπραξεν means 'did' generally, not specifically 'practiced'; 'inflicted' or 'wrought' better.
problems.fix: what he wrought against the many, this he endures from one.

problems.quote: For to defeat him would have brought him glory rather than shame
problems.source_quote: ἡττηθῆναι αὐτόν, δόξαν αὐτῷ μᾶλλον ἢ ὕβριν ἔφερεν
problems.why: Subject flipped: source says Christ's defeat would bring glory to devil, not devil's defeat.
problems.fix: For to be defeated by him would have brought him glory rather than shame.
problems.ruling: ἡττηθῆναι αὐτόν = 'his being defeated' (Christ's). English 'to defeat him' flips subject to devil.

problems.source_quote: ἐγὼ δι' αὐτοῦ παρέχω τὴν ἀνάστασιν
problems.why: αὐτοῦ refers back to σώματος (body), not death; Christ provides resurrection through his body.
problems.fix: through it [the body] I provide resurrection.
problems.ruling: αὐτοῦ refers to σώματος (body), not θάνατον; 'through it' ambiguously points to death, losing the body reference.

problems.source_quote: ὁ ποιμαίνων, γάρ φησιν, τὸν Ἰσραὴλ πρόσχες, ὁ ὁδηγῶν ὡσεὶ πρόβατον τὸν Ἰωσήφ
problems.why: LXX Psalm 79:2 (Hebrew 80:1) begins 'ὁ ποιμαίνων τὸν Ἰσραήλ, πρόσχες...'; citation should be Psalm 79:2 or Hebrew 80:1, not Psalm 80:1.
problems.ruling: LXX numbering is Psalm 79:2; 'Psalm 80:1' cites Hebrew numbering without specifying, misleading for LXX source.

problems.quote: For to be defeated by him would have brought him glory rather than shame
problems.source_quote: ἡττηθῆναι αὐτόν, δόξαν αὐτῷ μᾶλλον ἢ ὕβριν ἔφερεν

fixed: Changed 'For to be defeated by him' to 'For me to be defeated by him' to clarify that the subject is Christ being defeated, not the devil (source: ἡττηθῆναι αὐτόν, δόξαν αὐτῷ μᾶλλον ἢ ὕβριν ἔφερεν).
Changed 'through the body I provide resurrection' to 'through it I provide resurrection' because δι' αὐτοῦ refers back to death, not body (source: ἐγὼ δι' αὐτοῦ παρέχω τὴν ἀνάστασιν).

fixed.quote: For me to be defeated by him would have brought him glory rather than shame.
fixed.fix: For him to be defeated by me would have brought him glory rather than shame.
fixed.note: In ἡττηθῆναι αὐτόν, αὐτόν is the subject of the infinitive, so the devil is the one defeated; the English reverses who is beaten.

dismissed.quote: devising a deception that profits the world
dismissed.why: ἐπινοήσας modifies the devil's action of devising, but 'devising a deception' makes it sound intentional; he devised the trophy unwittingly.
dismissed.note: 'Devising a deception that profits the world' is a fair rendering of ἐπινοήσας; the irony is clear from 'by being deceived', and nothing in the wording makes the devil's aim sound deliberate.

dismissed.quote: fearful and lowly and weak flesh
dismissed.why: δειλῆς here means 'timid/cowardly' (cf. δειλία in glossary), not 'fearful'; the flesh is described as timid, not frightening.
dismissed.note: Here 'fearful' means timid or afraid, which matches δειλῆς; the checker's claim that it means 'frightening' does not hold.

dismissed.quote: condemn me for fear out of ignorance
dismissed.why: δι' ἄγνοιαν modifies the condemning (ignorantly condemn), not 'fear out of ignorance'.
dismissed.note: In English, 'out of ignorance' naturally attaches to 'condemn', so the syntax of δι' ἄγνοιαν is kept.
